answer: A harbour economy stays honest when every new identity must pass, in person, through a distinct vault door that opens for one applicant a day, proving a living pulse no recording can fake, and a custodian stakes their licence on each check. The first fake costs one vault visit, the tenth ten, and the twentieth twenty, so twenty invented agents would owe 210 days of queue. Bulk farming fails because vault doors are few, each admits one person at a time, and one operator cannot stand in twenty vaults at once, like a jetty that berths one boat at a time before it may unload.
